findings.finding: Man Wah Holdings (HKEX 1999), a sofa maker that counts DFS among its ten largest European customers, has built a DFS stake with its chairman from 3.17% to 10.18% since 30 Jun. It crossed 10% on 22 Sep, the day Yahoo shows 2.34m shares traded against a ~0.25m median. On 31 Aug the listed company bought 7.68m shares from the chairman's family vehicle at £1.623 a share, about 9% above spot, with a stated aim of a 'closer cooperative relationship'. A price-insensitive strategic buyer that is still active into the print cushions a disappointing guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior results day had a live strategic buyer in the register. On 16 Jul 2026 (H2 order intake -4.4%) the stock fell 5.99% while Man Wah's position sat at about 5%. The next day, 17 Jul, it recovered +7.1% (133.5 to 143.0 on Yahoo daily closes, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/DFS.L?range=4mo&interval=1d), and Man Wah crossed 6% on 29 Jul.

findings.why_not_priced: Only partly priced. The English-language record is a string of TR-1 forms with no commentary. I found no English article framing Man Wah as a strategic or possible bidder, and no mention that it paid 162.3p, above today's price. If the market read this as bid interest the stock would carry a premium to the 162p Man Wah paid. Instead it sits at 148.5, below that and below the 165 of late August. The one visible repricing is today's +7% intraday on 1.36m shares after the 09:05 TR-1, and that is why this is sized small: a good part of it is already in the window's opening price.
findings.independence: The TR-1 series on Investegate and the HKEX connected-transaction filing are separate documents from separate regulators. They show the same buyer, so this counts as one finding. https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0831/2026083100921.pdf

findings.finding: Container freight has roughly doubled into FY27, and DFS itself sizes that exposure: 'every $1,000 movement in freight rate per container impacts our annual freight cost charge by c.£7m-£8m a year'. Drewry Shanghai to Rotterdam ran $4,287-4,682 per FEU from July to August 2026 and $3,626 on 17 Sep, against $2,840 in January 2026, and the composite WCI stood at $1,669-1,959 in Oct-Nov 2025. So a $1,000-1,500 sustained gap is £7-12m against a FY27 consensus of £48.0m that assumes +7% PBT growth on +0.9% revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Freight turned from tailwind into a headwind within FY25: a -120bp gross-margin hit disclosed in the FY25 prelims (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/dfs-furniture--dfs/fy25-preliminary-results/9130219). The stock rose 2.0% that day because the company said it was 'comfortable with consensus'. The last time DFS's outlook disappointed (16 Jul 2026, weaker H2 demand) it fell 5.99%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, so sized small. The sensitivity is in DFS's own FY25 results and the freight index is public, so the sell-side can do this arithmetic. The company-compiled FY27 consensus was refreshed on 16 Sep, after the freight spike, and still shows +7% growth. So either analysts expect mitigation or rates to fall, which is happening: -9% on the week to 17 Sep as Suez reopens. If the market had priced a freight-driven FY27 cut, the FY27 consensus on DFS's own page would sit at or below FY26's £44.8m, not at £48.0m. The residual is a probability-weighted chance the new CFO (Dominique Highfield, on the board since 5 May 2026) guides below that number.
findings.independence: Drewry WCI via Daily Cargo News, 17 Sep 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-17-september-2026), 2 Jul 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-2-july-2026), 13 Aug 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-13-august-2026) and 8 Jan 2026 (https://www.thedcn.com.au/news/world-container-index-8-january-2026). This is a different source from the company sensitivity.

baseline_tension: Neither finding cuts clearly against the lean. The +0.3 lean and the -6% 20d run-up are overtaken by today's +7% intraday move on the Man Wah TR-1, which is my positive finding already partly priced. The freight headwind leans against the stock's 5d +4.6%. The two offset, so the emitted 0.0 sits on their -0.1 sum.
language_note: Domestic UK sources (RNS on Investegate, DFS's own IR pages) carried the full TR-1 sequence 3.17% to 10.18% and the company-compiled consensus. Reuters/TradingView syndicate the same TR-1s, so the domestic UK half added nothing on the facts that English wires lack. What it added was completeness: the whole series in one place, plus the 16 Sep consensus refresh.

What the UK and English sources did not carry came from Hong Kong, not from UK domestic sources: Chinese-language HK press (news.qq.com, caiwennews.com) and the HKEX connected-transaction filing gave the 162.3p price, the vendor (the chairman's family vehicle), the 'closer cooperative relationship' rationale and that DFS is a top-ten European customer of Man Wah. That is a third locality, outside the UK's local half, and I record it as such rather than crediting it to the UK domestic pass.
lessons_applied: 'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis' and 'a proxy that contradicts a broader public series loses': dropped the +0.4 consumer-confidence finding. GfK sentiment (up) is contradicted by BRC's actual August big-ticket furniture sales (down), and I have no company or counterparty document on DFS's own Q1 FY27 orders. Moved to searched_and_found_nothing.

'Keep findings inside the exit window': cut the Man Wah finding from +0.6 to +0.4 and moved its strategic or offer optionality to outside_window. Only the flow support falls inside the one-session bmo window.

'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number': the two remaining findings offset, and today's +7% spike means the positive one is partly in the opening price, so expected_move went from +0.3 to 0.0.
'A truncated zero is not evidence nobody is short': positioning_check now says anchor_covered is false and the lean is the run-up.
